decisions.reason: As a new safety shoe line in the firm’s core knowledge domain, it strongly builds on existing design, certification, production, and sales capabilities, so management would be likely to refine rather than withdraw it.

A comfort insole is closely related to the firm’s footwear expertise and customer base, but because it sits alongside other new insole variants it faces some portfolio-rationalisation risk if demand or differentiation proves weak.

The supportive insole also fits the firm’s absorptive capacity well, yet overlap with the other insole launches makes it somewhat more exposed to being merged or discontinued if early market feedback is mixed.

An ergonomic safety shoe series is highly aligned with the firm’s established protective-footwear knowledge and was given strong visibility, suggesting management sees enough learning and commercial potential to continue it.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised but still related extension of the firm’s protective-footwear capabilities, so they are likely to be kept unless the niche market response falls clearly short of expectations.

Because the moulded insole was presented as a flagship direction and is tightly connected to the firm’s footwear know-how, management would be very unlikely to drop it so early and would instead invest in improving it.
